subprocess: Third Party Inventory and Risk Tiering
risk: The organisation does not know who its third parties are or which matter, so oversight is applied to the wrong ones.
audit_objective: Confirm third parties are identified completely and tiered by the risk they present.
what_to_review: Completeness of the third-party register against payments and system access
Criticality and risk tiering methodology
Fourth-party and subcontracting visibility
Ownership of each relationship inside the business
Refresh of tiering when the service changes
procedures: Build an independent third-party inventory from accounts payable and system access data and compare it to the register.
Test the tiering of a sample against the methodology; challenge any critical service tiered low.
Test whether subcontracting by key providers is known and permitted by contract.
Test that each relationship has a named business owner.
red_flags: Providers paid regularly but absent from the register
Critical services tiered as low risk
No knowledge of who the provider subcontracts to
Relationships with no owner since the manager left
plain: You cannot manage suppliers you do not know you have, and most companies have more than they think.

risk: Third parties are engaged without checks on their financial health, integrity or capability, and problems surface only after dependency exists.
audit_objective: Confirm due diligence is performed before engagement and is proportionate to risk.
what_to_review: Due diligence scope by risk tier — financial, sanctions, integrity, capability
Timing — before contract signature or after
Sanctions, anti-bribery and modern slavery screening
Site visits or technical assessment for critical providers
Refresh of due diligence during the relationship
procedures: Test that due diligence was completed before contract signature for a sample of engagements.
Test screening evidence for sanctions and adverse media on critical providers.
Test the currency of due diligence for long-standing relationships.
Assess whether financial health of critical providers is monitored, not just checked once.
red_flags: Due diligence dated after the contract
Long relationships never re-assessed
Screening limited to a search engine query
Financial distress at a provider discovered from the news
plain: Checking a supplier after you depend on them is too late to do anything about what you find.

risk: Contracts omit the protections the organisation needs, so there is no remedy when the provider fails.
audit_objective: Confirm contracts contain the terms required for the risk the provider carries.
what_to_review: Presence of service levels, remedies and service credits
Audit and inspection rights
Data protection, confidentiality and security obligations
Liability caps, indemnities and insurance requirements
Termination, exit assistance and transition obligations
procedures: Review contracts for critical providers against a required-terms checklist and quantify gaps.
Test whether spend is occurring under expired or absent contracts.
Test whether liability caps are proportionate to the exposure the service creates.
Test whether audit rights have ever been exercised.
red_flags: Material spend with no signed contract
Liability capped at one month of fees for a critical service
Auto-renewal with no review point
Audit rights present but never used
plain: The contract is the only leverage you have when a supplier fails. Missing terms means no remedy.

risk: Provider performance is not measured, so service degrades and contractual remedies go unclaimed.
audit_objective: Confirm provider performance is measured against contract and managed actively.
what_to_review: Service level definition and who measures performance
Provider self-reporting versus independent measurement
Service credit and remedy claims
Governance meetings, minutes and escalation
Relationship between performance and contract renewal
procedures: Test whether performance data is produced by the provider or independently verified.
Recompute service levels for a sample of periods and test whether credits due were claimed.
Review governance meeting minutes for substance and escalation of persistent failures.
Test whether poor performers were renewed regardless.
red_flags: Performance reported solely by the provider
Service credits never claimed
Governance meetings cancelled repeatedly
Consistently failing providers renewed
plain: If nobody measures the service, it drifts, and the credits you were owed are never claimed.

risk: The organisation relies on controls operated by a third party without any evidence that they work.
audit_objective: Confirm assurance is obtained over provider controls and acted upon.
what_to_review: Assurance strategy by tier — service auditor reports, certifications, right to audit
Review of reports received, including exceptions and qualified opinions
Complementary user entity controls and whether they are performed
Coverage gaps between report period and financial year
Escalation of adverse findings
procedures: Obtain service auditor reports for critical providers; test whether anyone read them by tracing exceptions to management action.
Identify complementary user entity controls and test whether the organisation performs each.
Test the coverage period against the financial year and how gaps are addressed.
Assess reliance placed on certifications that do not cover the services actually used.
red_flags: Reports filed unread
Complementary controls never identified
Certification scope excluding the service used
Qualified opinions with no response
plain: When a supplier performs a control for you, you still have to prove it works.

risk: Third parties hold or access the organisation's data without adequate protection, and a breach at the provider becomes the organisation's breach.
audit_objective: Confirm data shared with third parties is protected, minimised and governed.
what_to_review: Inventory of data shared with each provider and its classification
Processor agreements and lawful basis for transfers
Security requirements imposed and verified
Provider access into the organisation's environment
Breach notification obligations and testing of the route
procedures: Reconcile providers receiving personal or sensitive data to signed processor agreements.
Test the security requirements imposed on providers and any verification performed.
Test provider access accounts — authentication, privilege, monitoring and removal.
Test whether breach notification routes have been exercised or are theoretical.
red_flags: Data shared with no agreement in place
Provider staff with standing privileged access
Security requirements stated but never verified
No test of the breach notification path
plain: A data breach at your supplier is reported as your data breach.

risk: A critical provider fails and there is no alternative and no exit plan, so the disruption is unbounded.
audit_objective: Assess whether dependency on third parties is understood and survivable.
what_to_review: Concentration analysis — single providers, shared fourth parties, geographic concentration
Business continuity requirements imposed and tested with the provider
Exit plans, transition assistance and data return
Substitutability of each critical provider
Testing of failover to an alternative
procedures: Identify critical services with a single provider and no substitute, and test the mitigation.
Test whether continuity arrangements have been jointly exercised with the provider.
Review exit plans for credibility — timescale, cost, data format, resource.
Analyse fourth-party concentration where several providers depend on the same underlying supplier.
red_flags: Exit plan consisting of a single paragraph
Continuity never tested with the provider
Several critical providers hosted on the same platform
Data held in a proprietary format with no export
plain: If a critical supplier fails and there is no alternative, the disruption lasts as long as it lasts.

risk: Work performed offshore creates regulatory, tax and resilience exposure that was never assessed.
audit_objective: Confirm cross-border service arrangements comply with regulatory and data residency requirements.
what_to_review: Regulatory notification or approval requirements for outsourcing
Data residency and cross-border transfer mechanisms
Local labour, tax and permanent establishment considerations
Time zone, language and oversight practicality
Geopolitical and country risk assessment
procedures: Test whether required regulatory notifications for outsourcing were made.
Test data residency against the contractual and regulatory requirement.
Assess whether offshore arrangements create permanent establishment or transfer pricing exposure.
Test the practical oversight exercised over offshore operations.
red_flags: Outsourcing arrangements never notified to the regulator
Data processed in jurisdictions not permitted
No country risk assessment for concentrated locations
Oversight limited to a monthly call
plain: Moving work to another country brings regulatory, tax and oversight issues that are easy to miss.

risk: The board and its committees lack the information, independence or challenge to oversee the organisation effectively.
audit_objective: Assess whether governance arrangements provide genuine oversight.
what_to_review: Board and committee composition, independence and skills
Quality, timeliness and balance of information provided
Evidence of challenge in minutes
Committee terms of reference and coverage of their remit
Board evaluation and succession planning
procedures: Review minutes across several meetings for evidence of challenge, dissent and follow-up, not just approval.
Test whether papers reached members with enough time to read them.
Test committee coverage against terms of reference — matters required but never discussed.
Assess whether management reporting to the board matches what the audit found operationally.
red_flags: Minutes recording approval with no discussion
Papers issued the day before
Terms of reference matters never on any agenda
Board evaluation never performed
evidence: Board and committee minutes and packs
plain: The board is the last line of defence. If it cannot see problems or will not challenge, nothing else compensates.

subprocess: Tone at the Top and Culture
risk: Stated values are contradicted by what management rewards and tolerates, so controls are undermined from above.
audit_objective: Assess whether the culture supports the control environment in practice, not only in policy.
what_to_review: Code of conduct, its communication and acknowledgement
Consistency between stated values and incentive design
Consequence management — how breaches by senior staff are handled
Speak-up culture and psychological safety indicators
Employee survey results relevant to ethics and pressure
procedures: Compare disciplinary outcomes for similar breaches at different seniority levels.
Test whether incentive plans reward outcomes the code discourages.
Review survey data for indicators of pressure to meet targets at any cost, and follow up on the worst-scoring units.
Interview staff at multiple levels about whether they would raise a concern and what they expect would happen.
red_flags: Senior breaches handled quietly while junior ones are dismissed
Targets that can only be met by cutting corners
Survey scores on ethics declining with no response
Exit interviews citing pressure repeatedly
evidence: Employee survey and exit interview data
plain: People take their cue from what leaders reward and tolerate, not from what the policy says.

risk: Risk management is a reporting exercise disconnected from decisions, so real risks are absent from the register.
audit_objective: Assess whether the risk framework identifies and manages the risks that actually threaten the organisation.
what_to_review: Risk appetite definition and its use in decisions
Risk identification process and register completeness
Assessment methodology and consistency of scoring
Mitigation ownership, action tracking and effectiveness
Emerging risk identification and horizon scanning
procedures: Compare the risk register to issues identified by audit, incidents and losses — gaps show the identification process is not working.
Test whether risk appetite has ever caused a decision to change.
Test the scoring of a sample for consistency and challenge.
Test whether mitigation actions were completed and made a difference.
red_flags: Risks scored to sit just inside appetite
Register unchanged for years
Incidents occurring in areas rated low risk
Mitigation actions perpetually in progress
plain: If the risk register does not contain the things that actually go wrong, risk management is decoration.

risk: Policies are out of date, contradictory or unknown to the people expected to follow them.
audit_objective: Confirm the policy framework is current, accessible and complied with.
what_to_review: Policy inventory, ownership and review cycle
Accessibility and communication to affected staff
Consistency between related policies
Attestation and training completion
Monitoring of actual compliance rather than assumed compliance
procedures: Test the policy inventory for overdue reviews and identify policies referencing superseded regulation.
Test staff awareness of key policies in the areas audited.
Test attestation and training completion, particularly for high-risk roles.
Compare policy requirements to observed practice in the processes audited.
red_flags: Policies years past review date
Practice diverging from policy with no exception recorded
Training completion tracked but not enforced
Contradictory requirements in related policies
plain: A policy nobody knows about or follows provides no protection, only the appearance of it.

risk: Authority limits are unclear, outdated or unenforced, so decisions are made by people without the mandate.
audit_objective: Confirm delegated authority is defined, current and enforced in the systems where it matters.
what_to_review: Currency of the delegation of authority matrix
Alignment between the matrix and system configuration
Delegation during absence and its expiry
Authority held by leavers and movers
Evidence of decisions taken outside authority
procedures: Compare the delegation matrix to system approval limits in the finance, procurement and HR systems and quantify differences.
Test delegations granted during absence for expiry.
Reconcile approvers active in systems to current role holders.
Test a sample of significant decisions against the authority held at the time.
red_flags: System limits inconsistent with the matrix
Temporary delegations never revoked
Leavers still active as approvers
Matrix last updated after a reorganisation two years ago
plain: If it is unclear who can approve what, decisions get made by people without the authority to make them.

risk: Fraud risk is assumed to be covered by other controls, so no one assesses where the organisation is actually exposed.
audit_objective: Assess whether fraud risk is specifically assessed, mitigated and detected.
what_to_review: Fraud risk assessment covering asset misappropriation, corruption and financial reporting fraud
Ownership of fraud risk and specific anti-fraud controls
Fraud detection analytics and their coverage
Investigation capability, independence and consistency
Loss recording, recovery and lessons applied
procedures: Test whether a fraud risk assessment exists and covers the schemes relevant to the business, not generic categories.
Test the anti-fraud controls claimed against each significant scheme.
Review investigations for independence, quality and consistency of outcome.
Test whether identified frauds led to control changes.
red_flags: Fraud risk assessment copied from a template
Investigations conducted by the function investigated
Losses written off without root cause work
No detective analytics in high-risk processes
plain: Fraud does not get prevented by general controls. Someone has to think specifically about how it would be done here.

risk: Concerns are not raised or not acted upon, and undisclosed interests influence decisions.
audit_objective: Assess whether the speak-up channel is trusted and effective and whether conflicts are managed.
what_to_review: Channel availability, anonymity, independence and awareness
Case triage, investigation independence and closure quality
Conflict of interest declarations — completeness and refresh
Management of declared conflicts, not just declaration
Retaliation monitoring
procedures: Analyse case volume against benchmarks for organisation size; very low volume indicates a channel people do not trust.
Test cases implicating senior management for investigator independence.
Reconcile conflict declarations to the population required to declare, particularly procurement, finance and hiring managers.
Test what happened after a conflict was declared — management action, not just a record.
red_flags: Case volume near zero
Cases closed as unsubstantiated with no documented work
Declarations collected but never acted on
Reporters leaving shortly after raising a concern
plain: If raising a concern feels unsafe, management finds out about problems from the regulator or the press instead.

risk: Regulatory obligations are not identified or tracked to an owner, so breaches are found by the regulator.
audit_objective: Confirm regulatory obligations are identified, owned, monitored and evidenced.
what_to_review: Completeness of the regulatory obligation inventory
Horizon scanning for new and changing requirements
Ownership and monitoring of each obligation
Breach identification, self-reporting and remediation
Regulatory relationship and correspondence handling
procedures: Build an obligation list independently for the most significant regulations and compare to the inventory.
Test evidence of compliance for a sample of obligations rather than an assertion.
Test breach self-reporting timeliness and remediation delivery.
Test whether regulatory change was assessed and implemented on time.
red_flags: Obligations with no owner
Compliance asserted with no evidence
Regulatory change implemented after the deadline
Breaches identified externally first
plain: Regulatory obligations that nobody owns get missed, and being told by the regulator is the expensive way to find out.

risk: The organisation cannot continue operating through disruption because plans are theoretical and untested.
audit_objective: Assess whether continuity and crisis arrangements would work in practice.
what_to_review: Business impact analysis and its currency
Continuity plans for critical processes, including dependencies
Testing — scope, realism and lessons captured
Crisis management structure, roles and decision authority
Communication plans for staff, customers and regulators
procedures: Test whether the business impact analysis reflects the current operating model.
Review the most recent continuity test for realism — was anything actually switched off?
Test whether lessons from previous tests or real incidents were implemented.
Assess whether plans account for third-party and technology dependencies.
red_flags: Plans referencing systems or premises no longer used
Tests that are desktop discussions only
Lessons logged but never actioned
Plans assuming staff availability during a regional event
plain: Plans that have never been tested tend not to work when they are finally needed.
